assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishes that liquid-liquid phase separation organizes cytoplasm and nucleus into membraneless compartments, a clear physical principle (demixing, surface tension, concentration thresholds) with quantitative support from P-granule, nucleolus and condensate work. It opened a large field in cell chemistry and disease, and it is generative in the sense of reframing how reaction compartments form.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the founding observations of liquid-like P granules (2009) and the nucleolus; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction framework with defined in vitro systems. Pappu and Mittag are important on sequence grammar and physics but are more naturally a refinement than the originating discovery.
assessment.maturity: Roughly fifteen years of independent confirmation; the principle is stable, though the physiological role of condensates versus artifacts of overexpression is still debated, which tempers timing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as cell biology/physiology.
Debate over how many reported condensates are true phase separation in vivo.
Fair credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity via bifunctional degraders and molecular glues gives a genuinely new capability: removing a target protein rather than inhibiting it, including previously undruggable targets. The concept is simple and the chemistry is original; clinical programs now give broad impact. It fits the 'previously unforeseen opportunities' criterion strongly.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs (2001) and the later small-molecule version; Ciulli contributed VHL-based design and structural rationale. Molecular glue degraders (Handa, Ito on thalidomide/cereblon) are a second strand that may need separate recognition, which complicates a three-person citation.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials and cereblon mechanism is well confirmed, but no approved PROTAC drug yet; recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with PROTAC and molecular-glue parts needing different credit.
Absence of an approved PROTAC drug.
Whether Handa/Ito/Sakamoto should displace Ciulli in the allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a mature, general method that changed how amines are attached to arenes in pharmaceuticals and materials. The mechanistic understanding (oxidative addition, amide binding, reductive elimination) is detailed and quantitative, and impact is lasting and widely used in industry.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic method and ligand design in the mid-1990s onward; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work was a precursor but not the general method. A two-laureate prize seems clean and defensible, which suits a broad-audience citation.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent use; this is arguably overdue and carries no maturity risk.
uncertainties: Treatment of Migita/Kosugi precedent and Louie contributions.
Committee may regard it as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single polymers by ionic current blockades, a physical principle I find compelling: single-molecule electrical detection at nanometer scale, now yielding long-read DNA/RNA sequencing. The chain from concept to commercial device is clear and quantitative.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Church proposed and explored the idea; Kasianowicz showed polynucleotide translocation through alpha-hemolysin; Bayley engineered pores; Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled DNA ratcheting that made sequencing work. Selecting three from this credited set is a real attribution difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Technology is widely deployed and confirmed; the interpretation is stable, and timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Hard allocation among Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson.
Whether the prize would be seen as analytical chemistry or biophysics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite solar cells reached high efficiencies within about a decade with solution processing, an unusual leap that opened a new class of absorbers. The physics of defect tolerance and long carrier diffusion is a rich fundamental topic.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells (2009); Park made the solid-state cell (2012), and Snaith the thin-film/meso-superstructured demonstration. Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok are strong alternates, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Stability and lead toxicity are unresolved and commercial maturity is not yet proven, so this may be premature.
uncertainties: Disputed credit among many strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a new capability grounded in deaminase chemistry and protein engineering, with clinical impact. Chemically distinct from the CRISPR cleavage prize of 2020.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental program; Komor (cytosine) and Gaudelli (adenine) were the first authors of the foundational papers. Liu alone is the most defensible core, but the credited set allows trainees.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is just beginning and the field is still evolving, with prime editing as a successor; recognition could be early.
uncertainties: Whether base and prime editing should be recognized together.
Doubts whether trainee credit is appropriate for a Nobel.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and programmable nanostructures show design rules for building arbitrary nanoscale objects from base pairing, a clean physical principle (thermodynamics and kinetics of hybridization). Wide uptake in nanotechnology, though applications beyond demonstration are still maturing.
assessment.attribution: Seeman founded structural DNA nanotechnology but is deceased and not in the supplied credit; Rothemund introduced origami (2006), Winfree developed algorithmic self-assembly and strand displacement, and Yin brick/tile methods. A fair triple exists but credit is uneven.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups; practical impact is still modest compared with the concept, so timing is uncertain.
uncertainties: Seeman's foundational role cannot be recognized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned potentials give near-quantum accuracy at force-field cost, opening simulations of long timescales and large systems; a clear methodological leap with broad use in materials and chemistry. The principle (symmetry-adapted regression of potential energy surfaces) is clean.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's 2007 neural-network potential and Bartók and Csányi's Gaussian approximation potentials are the two founding strands; Parrinello also appears elsewhere on the list, which complicates fair prize configuration.
assessment.maturity: The field is moving very quickly with foundation models; the specific lasting contribution may become clearer later, so this may be premature.
uncertainties: Rapid change in the field leaves lasting attribution unsettled.
Overlap of Parrinello with other candidates.
